edges.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal blood flow and lithium clearance, raising serum lithium; COX-2 inhibitor cases with rises up to 99% (celecoxib) and 448% (rofecoxib).
edges.evidence: FDA label Table 4; FAERS case series and literature review; Ontario case-control found no independent NSAID association with toxicity admissions. Documented at therapeutic doses; untested for supplemental doses.

edges.mechanism: Reduced renal lithium clearance (-25.5%) with steady-state lithium +36%; elderly most susceptible.
edges.evidence: Retrospective study (n=20); population case-control: toxicity admission RR 7.6 within a month of starting; label warning.

edges.mechanism: Renin-angiotensin antagonists increase steady-state serum lithium.
edges.evidence: FDA label class warning; review of 30 intoxication reports implicating RAS inhibitors.

edges.mechanism: Diuretic-induced sodium loss increases proximal lithium reabsorption; 25-40% rise in lithium after initiation.
edges.evidence: Pharmacokinetic review and label; Ontario case-control did not find independent association with admissions.

edges.mechanism: Volume contraction after furosemide reduces lithium clearance.
edges.evidence: Population case-control: toxicity admission RR 5.5 within a month of starting; human physiology study.

edges.mechanism: Additive serotonergic effect; lithium can precipitate serotonin syndrome.
edges.evidence: FDA label warning; case report with venlafaxine (Naranjo probable).

edges.mechanism: Increase renal lithium clearance (~30%), lowering serum lithium and risking loss of efficacy.
edges.evidence: Human pharmacokinetic study; label lists xanthine preparations as lowering lithium.

edges.mechanism: Caffeine increases lithium clearance; abrupt caffeine withdrawal raised lithium and worsened tremor.
edges.evidence: Two case reports; consistent with methylxanthine pharmacokinetics.

edges.mechanism: Low salt intake and volume depletion reduce lithium clearance; add-on 1 g/d NaCl reduced serum lithium fluctuation (26.7% vs 63.3%).
edges.evidence: Human physiology study; RCT (n=60); label warning on dehydration and hyponatremia.

edges.mechanism: Reports of neurotoxicity ranging from extrapyramidal symptoms to neuroleptic malignant syndrome and encephalopathy.
edges.evidence: FDA label (case reports).

edges.mechanism: May decrease serum lithium concentrations.
edges.evidence: FDA label.

edges.mechanism: Iodide and lithium both inhibit thyroid hormone release; combined use can produce hypothyroidism (or Jod-Basedow hyperthyroidism).
edges.evidence: Label warning; study of 10 lithium-treated patients given KI 250 mg qid: TSH +8.9 uU/mL, 2 hypothyroid, 1 hyperthyroid. Pharmacological iodide doses; relevance to nutritional iodine unknown.

edges.mechanism: Conflicting reports: no effect or decreased lithium in some reports, increases in others.
edges.evidence: Literature review within FAERS/NSAID analysis.

edges.mechanism: Oral magnesium sulfate did not alter lithium carbonate absorption despite purgative effect.
edges.evidence: Single small human study (n=10); essentially no interaction found.

edges.mechanism: Lithium raises serum calcium and PTH and causes hyperparathyroidism; calcium-raising supplements could add to or mask lithium-associated hypercalcemia.
edges.evidence: Inferred from MA data on lithium; no direct combination study.

edges.mechanism: Renal elimination; impaired clearance raises toxicity risk; lithium itself associated with CKD3+ (HR 1.90; dose-dependent).
edges.evidence: Label: avoid at CrCl<30 mL/min; nationwide cohorts.

edges.mechanism: First-trimester exposure increases cardiac malformations including Ebstein anomaly (aRR 1.65; >900 mg/d RR 3.22) and any malformation (OR 1.81).
edges.evidence: Cohort of 1.3M pregnancies; MAs; label. Data are for therapeutic doses.

edges.mechanism: Infant plasma lithium 30-40% of maternal; toxicity signs reported in breastfed infants.
edges.evidence: FDA label.

edges.mechanism: Lithium inhibits thyroid hormone synthesis/release; hypothyroidism OR 5.78; occasional hyperthyroidism.
edges.evidence: SR/MA, cohort, SR of hyperthyroidism cases.

edges.mechanism: Lithium raises calcium and PTH; lithium-associated HPT ~4-5%, often multiglandular.
edges.evidence: SR/MAs.

edges.mechanism: Lithium may unmask Brugada syndrome with risk of sudden death; bradycardia also reported.
edges.evidence: FDA label postmarketing reports; SR of 135 bradycardia cases.

edges.mechanism: Reduced renal clearance; toxicity signs at 0.82-1.00 mmol/L; drug interactions (diuretics, ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs) more hazardous.
edges.evidence: ISBD task force SR of 14 observational studies; population case-control.

edges.mechanism: Lithium heparin anticoagulant contaminates samples, giving spurious serum lithium (up to 4.19 mmol/L) and spuriously high enzymatic creatinine when tubes are underfilled.
edges.evidence: Case reports and laboratory experiment.

edges.mechanism: True physiological effects: TSH rises and neutrophilic leukocytosis occurs during lithium therapy; interpret thyroid and CBC results accordingly.
edges.evidence: SR/MA; RCT in MCI; cross-sectional study.
